svg.aria-label: Fig 3. Planned appeal writer. Facts and a fictional payer policy go to an LLM writer. The planned model is Muse. A citation gate checks that each statement cites a chunk ID. A red track takes a draft with an uncited statement back to the writer. Green tracks take the draft to tier 2 human approval and then to the send tray.
svg.title: Fig 3. Planned appeal writer. Facts and a fictional payer policy go to an LLM writer. The planned model is Muse. A citation gate checks that each statement cites a chunk ID. A red track takes a draft with an uncited statement back to the writer. Green tracks take the draft to tier 2 human approval and then to the send tray.
svg.text: Fictional payer policy. Design from the research docs, not yet decided. Not built.
no citation, no letter · no approval, no send
1 Inputs: the synthetic denial record, the facts from the record, and retrieved chunks
of a fictional payer policy (example payer ZZP01).
2 An LLM drafts the letter from the facts and the policy chunks. The planned model is Muse (D-011, proposed).
3 The citation gate checks that each statement maps to a retrieved chunk ID.
If a statement has no source, the draft goes back to the writer (red track).
4 A human approves the letter in the review console (tier 2). In the hackathon,
5 The appeal goes out only after approval. Then the voice agent follows up.
Small text on the parts (IDs, tags) is an example. The legend gives the facts.
black: 1 to 2 (the facts), 2 to 3 (the draft). red: 3 to 2 (a statement has no source).
green: 3 to 4 (all statements cited), 4 to 5 (the human approved).
